extracted.intended_audience: federal agency standards executives / policy and legal staff preparing OMB Circular A-119 reports
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing the agency response/reportation required by OMB Circular A-119 on federal participation in and use of voluntary consensus standards, including counts of participation, standards adopted, substitutions, evaluations of proposed Circular revisions, and explanations when government-unique standards were used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of voluntary consensus standards bodies and employee participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the number of voluntary consensus standards bodies in which the agency participates and the number of agency employees participating (e.g., "The Department participated in ten voluntary consensus standards bodies that accounted for approximately twenty-five employees participating.").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide counts and, where helpful, break down participation by office/office function and by named standards organizations (ANSI, ASTM, IEEE, etc.). Include contact person(s) for standards activity (name, title, phone, fax, email) as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of voluntary consensus standards used since Oct 1, 1996 (or per Section 8 procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: State how many voluntary consensus standards the agency has used during the reporting period (or under the procedures in Section 8 of the proposed Circular revision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the specific standards adopted (with citations/dates) where relevant; indicate none if none were used. Where adoption occurred, note the rulemaking or program context in which the standard was used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of voluntary standards substituted for government-unique standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify voluntary consensus standards that have been substituted for government-unique standards as a result of an agency review of existing standards (or as outlined under paragraph 7c(6) of the proposed revision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the substituted standard(s), the government-unique standard replaced, the regulatory provisions affected (citations/sections), and a short explanation of the substitution (e.g., USCG substitutions of NFPA 13-1996 and UL 1191 in specified sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of effectiveness of Section 7 guidelines and recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an evaluation of the effectiveness of the guidelines in Section 7 of the proposed revision to the Circular and any recommendations for changes (e.g., "We believe the guidelines in Section 7 ... are effective.").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer actionable recommendations for improving the Circular's guidance or implementation procedures; state whether the proposed guidelines would have side effects on the agency's goals and operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: When agency used government-unique standards instead of voluntary consensus standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Report instances where the agency used government-unique standards in lieu of voluntary consensus standards and explain why (e.g., none, or specific instances such as NHTSA air bag warning label or USCG tank-monitoring devices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each instance, explain the factual/technical reasons (e.g., focus group testing showing unique requirements are more effective, no existing voluntary standard for the technology) and document how the decision was explained in the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory requirement to publish reasons when a rule differs from a national consensus standard (OSHA §6(b)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a rule promulgated by the Secretary differs substantially from an existing national consensus standard, the Secretary shall publish in the Federal Register a statement of the reasons why the rule as adopted will better effectuate the purposes of this Act than the national consensus standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a clear, contemporaneous statement of reasons in the regulatory preamble when diverging from national consensus standards; cite the statute and provide the comparative justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-year (or ongoing) review to consider replacing government-unique standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct consistent examination of regulations (five-year review cycle or comprehensive review) to identify government-unique standards that can be replaced by voluntary consensus standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document review cycles, list standards replaced as a result of the five-year review, and indicate planned timelines for pending rulemakings to adopt voluntary standards (e.g., RSPA's planned rulemakings to substitute standards within 4–6 months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Track committee membership and employee participation (administrative tracking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain records of committee membership listings and employee participation in voluntary consensus standards groups (e.g., USCG Headquarters Notice 5420 to keep track of committee membership).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement systems (e.g., department-wide database) to record participation, facilitate timely review of standards, and coordinate agency involvement across offices and rulemakings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider incorporation by reference and international harmonization where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate and use voluntary consensus technical standards, including incorporation by reference, to reduce duplication, save time and money, and harmonize with international standards when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document instances where incorporation by reference was used; describe international standardization participation and efforts to shape/adopt standards abroad (e.g., Department efforts in ITU/ISO/CITEL).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain agency-specific reasons for departing from industry standards (testing, safety, absence of standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: When choosing government-unique requirements over industry standards, agencies should explain the rationale—examples include empirical testing showing greater effectiveness (NHTSA focus group testing) or the absence of a voluntary standard (USCG tank-monitoring devices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include detailed explanations and supporting evidence in the final rulemaking record (testing results, stakeholder input) and describe alternatives considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify standards adopted to promote environmentally sound and energy-efficient practices
rubrics_metrics.description: List voluntary standards adopted for promoting environmentally sound and energy-efficient materials, products, systems, services or practices (e.g., Energy Star–qualifying equipment, APCO 25 radio efficiency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate the public-law or executive-order context (e.g., Public Law 102-486; Executive Orders 12759, 12845) that motivates adoption and note any relevant Federal IRM regulations or bulletins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe nature and extent of departmental participation in standards development
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the agency's roles in standards development (voting membership, chairs of task groups, participation on boards, accreditation, sponsorship, co-sponsorship) and list specific committees/organizations involved (ASC X12, NACHA, Project-25, IEEE groups, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide organizational breakdowns (which bureaus/offices participate in which committees), the positions held (chair, co-chair, voting member), and the reasoning for participation (to advocate for agency business needs, to influence interoperable open standards).
